summary: This clipped web page from the American Tree Farm System (ATFS) describes its forest certification program for family forest landowners in the United States. It explains that ATFS, begun in 1941, offers third-party certification verified through the ATFS Verification Database, which mills and wood dealers can use to confirm sustainability. The page lists three certification options (State Tree Farm Committee programs, Independently Managed Group programs, and individual third-party certificates) and notes that ATFS land supplies chain-of-custody programs such as SFI and PEFC.
one_line: An overview of the American Tree Farm System's third-party forest certification for US family forest landowners, including its three certification options.
key_facts: The American Tree Farm System (ATFS) offers affordable forest certification for family forest landowners in the United States.
ATFS began promoting responsible forest management on the nation's private forests in 1941.
ATFS certification is shown exclusively through listing of a forest in the ATFS Verification Database.
ATFS-certified family forests meet eight standards of sustainability and are managed for water, wildlife, wood and recreation.
ATFS offers three ways to join the over 19 million acres of certified forestlands.
There are 42 active state committees working with 12.5 million acres on 38,000 Tree Farms across the U.S. under State Tree Farm Committee programs.
The Independently Managed Group (IMG) program was started in 2002 and currently has 12 IMGs certifying nearly 4.8 million acres.
An IMG program is facilitated by a group manager who oversees landowner entry and exit and coordinates certification audits.
Individual family forest owners seeking their own third-party certification should contract directly with a qualified certification body and undergo certification audits every three years.
Land certified by the American Tree Farm System is a principal source of fiber for the Sustainable Forestry Initiative (SFI, Inc.) and PEFC chain of custody programs.
ATFS is described as the United States' oldest family forest certification program.
ATFS is a program of the American Forest Foundation (AFF), headquartered at 2000 M Street, NW, Suite 550, Washington, D.C. 20036.
